newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices unchanged, awaiting U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices unchanged, awaiting U.S. data.

text.p: Danish bond prices opened largely unchanged on Tuesday, with little movement expected before the afternoon's U.S. consumer confidence data.
"The American numbers could change the picture but otherwise it will be a quiet day," a dealer said.
At 0710 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded at 111.90, yielding 6.19 percent, barely altered from Monday's 111.91.
The seven percent 2007,due to become the benchmark on September 1, opened unchanged at 104.49 then dipped to 104.46, yielding 6.39 percent.
The 2006 bond's yield gap to the 10-year bund narrowed to 44 basis points from Monday's 45. The 2007 gap to the bund also closed by one basis point, to 64 b.p.
The crown weakened slightly, to 3.8086 to the mark, from Monday's 3.8084. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
